recipes.title: Peruvian chicken quinoa soup, light
recipes.summary: A bright Peruvian-style soup with tender chicken, quinoa, potatoes and vegetables in a cumin-scented broth. Extra vegetables and less quinoa keep the bowl light but satisfying.

steps.instruction: Prepare the chicken thigh, potato, carrot, celery, onion, garlic, cilantro and lime in their listed sizes.
Rinse the quinoa under cold water until the water runs clear.
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat.
Brown the chicken thigh lightly around the edges.
Cook the onion, carrot and celery until the onion is soft and translucent.
Add the garlic, cumin and paprika and stir until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, canned, chicken broth and potato and bring the soup to a gentle simmer.
Simmer the soup until the potato and chicken thigh are nearly tender.
Add the quinoa and simmer until the grains are tender and their small spirals are visible.
Finish the soup with the cilantro and serve it with the lime.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat until steaming, adding chicken broth if the quinoa has absorbed too much liquid. Freeze for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Peruvian chicken quinoa soup
recipes.summary: A comforting Peruvian chicken and quinoa soup with potatoes, carrots, celery, tomatoes and fresh cilantro. Lime brightens the warm cumin and paprika broth.

steps.instruction: Prepare the chicken thigh, potato, carrot, celery, onion, garlic, cilantro and lime in their listed sizes.
Rinse the quinoa under cold water until the water runs clear.
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat.
Brown the chicken thigh until lightly coloured on several sides.
Cook the onion, carrot and celery until softened and fragrant.
Add the garlic, cumin and paprika and stir until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, canned, chicken broth and potato and bring the soup to a simmer.
Simmer the soup until the potato and chicken thigh are nearly tender.
Add the quinoa and simmer until the grains are tender and the broth looks lightly thickened.
Finish the soup with the cilantro and serve it with the lime.

recipes.storageNotes: Keep refrigerated for up to 3 days and loosen with chicken broth when reheating. Heat until steaming throughout. Freeze in portions for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Peruvian chicken quinoa soup, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous pot of Peruvian chicken quinoa soup with extra chicken, potatoes and grains. Cilantro and lime keep the substantial lunch fresh and aromatic.

steps.instruction: Prepare the chicken thigh, potato, carrot, celery, onion, garlic, cilantro and lime in their listed sizes.
Rinse the quinoa under cold water until the water runs clear.
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat.
Brown the chicken thigh in batches until lightly coloured.
Cook the onion, carrot and celery until completely softened.
Add the garlic, cumin and paprika and stir until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, canned, chicken broth and potato and bring the larger pot to a simmer.
Simmer the soup until the chicken thigh and potato are nearly tender.

Finish the soup generously with the cilantro and serve it with the lime.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and add chicken broth during reheating as needed. Freeze cooled portions for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Polish meatballs with mushroom sauce, light
recipes.summary: Tender beef meatballs with creamy mushroom and thyme sauce, served over soft potatoes. Less bread, butter and sour cream keep the high-protein dinner lighter.

steps.instruction: Prepare the potato, onion and mushrooms before mixing the meatballs.
Simmer the potato until completely tender when pierced with a knife.
Soak the bread in the whole milk until soft.
Mix the ground beef, eggs, soaked bread, paprika and half the onion until evenly combined.
Shape the ground beef mixture into evenly sized meatballs.
Melt the butter in a wide frying pan over medium heat.
Brown the meatballs on several sides until a golden crust forms.
Cook the remaining onion and mushrooms until soft and golden.
Stir the beef stock, sour cream and thyme into the mushrooms.
Simmer the meatballs in the mushroom sauce until cooked through.
Mash the potato and serve it with the meatballs and mushroom sauce.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat gently until the meatballs are hot throughout. Freeze the meatballs and sauce for up to 2 months; prepare fresh potatoes after thawing.

recipes.title: Polish meatballs with mushroom sauce, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous Polish-style dinner with extra beef meatballs, potatoes and creamy mushroom sauce. The substantial shared pan is deeply savoury and high in protein.

Shape the ground beef mixture into generous, evenly sized meatballs.

Mash the potato and serve it generously with the meatballs and mushroom sauce.

recipes.title: Peanut butter oat bars, light
recipes.summary: Soft-baked American oat bars with banana, peanut butter, cinnamon and sesame seeds. Less peanut butter and sugar keep the vegan snack lighter without making it dry.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 180°C and line a square baking tin.
Mash the banana until mostly smooth with only a few small pieces remaining.
Stir the peanut butter, brown sugar and cinnamon into the banana.
Fold the rolled oats and sesame seeds into the banana mixture until evenly moistened.
Press the oat mixture firmly and evenly into the lined tin.
Bake until the edges are golden and the centre feels set when lightly pressed.
Cool the peanut butter oat bars completely in the tin so they firm up.
Cut the slab into six even servings.

recipes.storageNotes: Keep refrigerated in a sealed container for up to 5 days. Freeze individual bars for up to 2 months and thaw at room temperature or overnight in the refrigerator.

recipes.title: Peanut butter oat bars
recipes.summary: Chewy American oat bars baked with ripe banana, peanut butter, brown sugar, cinnamon and sesame seeds. They make a simple vegan snack for meal prep.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 180°C and line a square baking tin.
Mash the banana until mostly smooth with only a few soft pieces remaining.
Stir the peanut butter, brown sugar and cinnamon into the banana until smooth.
Fold the rolled oats and sesame seeds into the banana mixture until evenly combined.
Press the oat mixture firmly and evenly into the lined tin.
Bake until the edges are golden and the centre is fully set.
Cool the peanut butter oat bars completely so they become chewy and easy to slice.
Cut the slab into six even servings.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 5 days in a sealed container. Freeze separated bars for up to 2 months and thaw before eating.

recipes.title: Peanut butter oat bars, hearty
recipes.summary: Thick vegan oat bars with extra peanut butter, banana and oats for a substantial American snack. Cinnamon and sesame seeds add a warm, nutty finish.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 180°C and line a deep square baking tin.
Mash the banana until smooth and creamy.
Stir the peanut butter, brown sugar and cinnamon into the banana until fully combined.
Fold the rolled oats and sesame seeds into the banana mixture until no dry oats remain.
Press the thick oat mixture firmly and evenly into the lined tin.
Bake until deeply golden at the edges and firm in the centre.
Cool the peanut butter oat bars completely in the tin so the thick slab sets.
Cut the slab into six generous servings.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate in a sealed container for up to 5 days. Freeze individual bars for up to 2 months and thaw overnight for the best texture.

recipes.title: Bubble and squeak with eggs, light
recipes.summary: A lighter British breakfast cake of crisp potatoes, cabbage and onion topped with softly cooked eggs. Extra cabbage keeps the pan generous while the butter stays restrained.

steps.instruction: Prepare the potato, green cabbage, onion and spring onions in their listed sizes.
Simmer the potato until completely tender when pierced with a knife.
Melt the butter in a wide non-stick frying pan over medium heat.
Cook the onion until soft and translucent.
Add the green cabbage and cook until tender and lightly browned at the edges.
Mash the potato until mostly smooth with a few small pieces remaining.
Mix the potato with the green cabbage and onion.
Press the mixture into the pan and cook until the underside is crisp and golden.
Turn the bubble and squeak and cook the second side until golden.
Make four shallow wells and crack the eggs into them.
Cover the pan and cook until the egg whites are set and the yolks remain tender.
Finish the bubble and squeak with eggs with the spring onions.

recipes.storageNotes: Best served immediately while the potato is crisp and the eggs are tender. Refrigerate leftovers for up to 2 days and reheat gently. Do not freeze the finished dish.

recipes.title: Bubble and squeak with eggs, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous British breakfast with extra crisp potatoes and six eggs over buttery cabbage and onion. Spring onions add a fresh finish to the substantial skillet.

steps.instruction: Prepare the potato, green cabbage, onion and spring onions in their listed sizes.
Simmer the potato until completely tender when pierced with a knife.
Melt the butter in a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat.
Cook the onion until soft and lightly golden.
Add the green cabbage and cook until tender and browned around the edges.
Mash the potato until mostly smooth while retaining some texture.
Mix the potato thoroughly with the green cabbage and onion.
Press the mixture into the pan and cook until the underside is deeply crisp and golden.
Turn the bubble and squeak and cook the second side until crisp.
Make six shallow wells and crack the eggs into them.
Cover the pan and cook until the egg whites are set and the yolks reach your preferred consistency.

recipes.title: Cuban pork and black bean stew, light
recipes.summary: A lighter Cuban-style stew with pork loin, black beans, peppers and tomatoes, served with a modest portion of rice. Cumin and paprika give the broth a warm savoury depth.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Prepare the pork loin, cured pork, onion, bell pepper and garlic in their listed sizes.
Cook the white rice until tender, then keep it covered so the grains finish steaming.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Brown the pork loin lightly on several sides.
Cook the cured pork until its edges begin to colour.
Cook the onion and bell pepper until softened and lightly golden.
Add the garlic, cumin and paprika and stir until fragrant.
Add the black beans, tomatoes, canned, beef stock and browned pork loin.
Simmer the stew gently until the pork loin is tender and the broth has thickened.
Rest the Cuban pork and black bean stew off the heat so the flavours settle.
Serve the stew with the white rice.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate the stew and rice separately for up to 4 days. Reheat until steaming. Freeze the stew without the rice for up to 3 months.

recipes.summary: A generous Cuban-style lunch with extra pork, black beans and rice in a thick tomato and pepper broth. Cured pork adds a deep savoury finish to the shared pot.
